datafield.subfield: Efficient metalcutting requires using the right shaped tool for the task. These tools are all described by their angles or geometries. To better understand these ables, this videotape examines: single point turning tool and toolholder geometries, milling and multi-point tool geometries, chipbreakers and the formation of chips.

Because of the wide variety of machining applications, there is a need for diverse cutting tool materials. To provide a broad understanding of these materials, this videotape examines: carbide and coated carbide tool materials, high speed steel, ceramic, cermet and superhard cutting tool applications, tool failure modes.

Grinding is a material removal process used to shape and finish high precision workpieces made from metals and nonmetals. To provide a broad understanding of grinding and its fundamentals components, this video examines: the four primary grinding processes, abrasives and grinding wheels, balancing, trueing and dressing grinding wheels, grinding safety, workpiece surface finish.

Casting is the solidification of molten metal that is poured into a mold, or injected into a die having a cavity in the shape of the desired part. Casting is usually the quickest way to shape metal into a part, and is used both for prototyping and large quantity production. This program covers an array of casting processes, arranging them into three major categories: expendalbe mold/reusable pattern processes, permanent mold/no pattern processes. Pattern and core production methods are also demonstrated.

Punch presses cut round and irregular-shaped holes in a variety of materials. In addition to punching, these presses are also capable of certain forming operations. Punch presses provide an economical means to quickly process parts that are used for manufacturing appliances, automotive components and other products. To provide a broad understanding of puch presses, this video examines: the punching process, single and turret punch presses, punching operations, including nibbling, tooling advances for punch presses

Two of the most basic operations in all of metalworking are shearing and bending. Shearing is the cutting of sheet metal by means of two opposing blades. Bending is the creation of three-dimensional shapes out of two-dimensional sheet metal or plate material. To better understand these processes, this program examines: the shearing process, the various shearing machines, the importance of gaging for shearing and bending, the principal terms used to describe a bend, the press brake and bending dies.

Stamping presses provide the force to open and close dies, which shape and cut sheet metal parts. Stamping presses vary widely in size, from bench top presses to extremely large tandem line presses. To provide an understanding of press types and their various applications, this videotape examines: mechanical gap-frame & straightside presses, components of the mechanical press, hydraulic presses, press controls & feeding methods

Stamping dies are tools that work inside presses to shape and cut sheet metal into functional parts. Stamping dies consist of upper and lower die assemblies, and can take many forms, shapes, and sizes. To better understand how stamping dies operate, this videotape examines: sheet metal formability, basic cutting and forming processes, die lubrication types & methods, stamping analysis techniques

Workholding includes any device used to grip and present a workpiece to a cutting tool on a machine tool. To provide an understanding of workholding as an fundamental issue in the machining process, this video examines: the principles of workholding, basic to advanced workholding approaches for milling and machining centers, collet, chucks and other lathe workholding devices.

Design for manufacture and assembly (DFMA) is a proven design methodology used to optimize part costs and quality, while reducing time-to-market development. This program features an interview with Nicholas Dewhurst of Boothroyd Dewhurst and explains the concepts and use of DFMA in product analysis to understand the drivers of cost, and the interaction of the individual pieces within the product to optimize design, manufacturability, and assembly.

This Manufacturing Insights program explores advancements in Direct Metal Manufacturing and shows how these technologies affect the creation of parts and tooling in various metals. It illustrates what happens when innovative companies capitalize on Direct Metal Manufacturing to make dramatic changes to the way parts and tooling are designed.

To provide a broad understanding of threads and threasing processes, this videotape examines: The various thread dimensions, external thread cutting and rollling processes, internal threads and tapping operations.

Program focuses on the primary machining and assembly processes used for plastics. The plastics machining segment highlights: sawing; milling; routing; drilling and secondary holemarking operations; turning; waterjet cutting; and laser cutting. The plastics assembly section cover: snap-fit fasteneners; the use of hinges; mechanical fasteners; adhesive and solvent bonding; and the various plastic welding processes.

Molds determine the shape of the part, vent trapped air or gases during injection, they act as heat exchangers to solidify the molten plastic, and they eject the cooled parts. Using shop floor footage and detailed animations, this program highlights the primary injection mold components, and features segments on: injection mold types, the use of computer simulation to develop molds, mold prototyping techniques, mold maintenance & repair.

Plastic blow molding processes are the most popular methods used to produce hollow products out of thermoplastics materials. Bottles and containers are the most common products, but other such as automotive components, toys, and medical items are also produced. Blow molding processes utilize a wide range of plastic resins, using a variety of production methods. These methods include: intermittent extrusion blow molding, continuous extrusion blow molding, injection blow molding, single-stage biaxial stretch blow molding, two-stage biaxial stretch blow molding, co-extrusion blow molding.

Turning on the lathe is one of the most common metal-cutting operations. In fact, the engine lathe is often the first machine a machinist learns to operate. to provide a broad understanding of the process, this videotape examines: the basic elements that comprise the engine lathe, lathe operations and process variables, manual through computer numerical control lathe types, tooling and workholding arrangements on production lathes.

Milling has more variations in machine design, tooling and workpiece movement than any other machining process. This videotape explores these variables, providing a basic understanding of the following subjects : the knee mill and its components, milling machines and machining centers, basic millings cutters and operations, workholding, workchanging, toolchangers and accessories, the milling process and operating parameters.
